abstract: |
  Urban agriculture is promoted as a climate-smart lever for food security, yet its spatial pattern and local food-security linkage remain under-quantified in Nigeria. This paper freezes verifiable open data — 484 OpenStreetMap allotment/farmland/garden footprints (Abuja 32, Lagos 130, Kano 189, Port Harcourt 88, Gombe 45), World Bank urban population and food-production indices (2000–2024; 75 rows) and NASA POWER daily climate (5 cities × 365 d, 2023) — and applies spatial statistics at LGA level (GADM 4.1, 775 LGAs). Global Moran's I on urban-agriculture counts is 0.158 (z=8.47, p<0.001) and on density (points km⁻²) is 0.300 (z=17.6, p<0.001), indicating strong spatial clustering. LISA identifies high-high clusters in Kano metropolis (Ungogo 90 pts, Tarauni 25, Kumbotso 17) and Obio/Akpor (Rivers, 64 pts) and low-low surrounds in savanna LGAs. Climate contrasts are sharp (annual rainfall 404 mm Kano vs 1,891 mm Port Harcourt). Results support spatially-targeted allotment zoning and compost-loop circularity as two policy levers bridging urban and rural food systems.

# Introduction

Urban agriculture — dry-season fadama, peri-urban farmland and intra-urban allotments — is positioned as a climate-smart lever for food security amid rapid urbanisation [@orhevba2024; @abubakar2023]. Nigeria's urban pop. 146.5M in 2024 (>55% [@worldbank2024]) outpaces infrastructure [@udoh2022].

Evidence remains aspatial: surveys rarely georeference sites and food-security metrics mask intra-urban heterogeneity [@adeleye2024], limiting translation into zoning, fadama protection and compost loops (sub-themes 6/10/13). The National Urban Policy (2022) prioritises compact cities but lacks LGA evidence — a gap addressed here.

We address this by (i) freezing OSM footprints with provenance (16 entries) [@openstreetmap2024], (ii) applying Moran/LISA and lag/error regression (Eqs. @eq-moran–@eq-error) [@pebesma2023; @bivand2023; @anselin1995], and (iii) translating clusters ($I=0.300$, $p<0.001$) into zoning insights.

# Study Area and Data

Five cities (Abuja, Lagos, Kano, Port Harcourt, Gombe) span 404–1,891 mm rainfall and 25.9–27.3°C (Table 2), providing a gradient for H2; LGAs (GADM v4.1, 775) are the areal unit [@gadm2022]. Data were frozen via one-time queries (`ds-general` Python 3.12) to `data/raw/*.csv` with `provenance.json` (16 entries) ensuring reproducibility.

| Layer | Source | Endpoint | Retained | $n$ |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Urban-ag footprints | OSM Overpass | `https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter` | `landuse` allotments/farmland/farmyard, `leisure` garden (dedup. `type+id`) | 484 |
| Population/food | World Bank WDI | `.../NG/indicator/{SP.URB.TOTL,AG.PRD.FOOD.XD,SN.ITK.DEFC.ZS}` | Pop., food index, undernourishment % | 75 |
| Climate | NASA POWER AG | `.../power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/daily/point?community=AG` | T2M, PRECTOTCORR, RH2M (daily 2023) | 1,825 |
| Boundaries | GADM v4.1 | `.../gadm41_NGA_shp.zip` | LGA polygons | 775 |
| Food stub | FAOSTAT | `.../faostat/api/v1/en/data/FS` → 521 → stub | `fao_food_security.csv` | 1 |

FAOSTAT 521 → 1-row stub retained (see `data/external/README.md`). World Bank series are national aggregates → used as contextual covariates; DHS/NLSS subnational undernourishment is the extension [@adeleye2024].

# Methods

## Design and hypotheses

We adopt a spatial-observational design [@bivand2023]. H1: density is clustered ($I>0$, Eq. @eq-moran); H2: density increases with aridity (lower PRECTOT, higher T2M); H3: density declines with LGA area ($\log(\text{area})$ negative in Eqs. @eq-lag–@eq-error) [@muhammed2022].

## Spatial descriptive

Density $=n/\text{area}_{km^2}$ with $\text{area}_{km^2}=\text{st\_area}/10^6$ (`sf` GEOS) corrects ten-fold LGA variation (11.6–10,358 km², median 697 km²); $I$ rises 0.158→0.300 upon normalisation (§Results). Kernel/G(r) omitted for page limit.

## Spatial dependence — formal tests

Let $\mathbf{x} = (x_1,\dots,x_N)^\top$ be density (or counts) on $N=775$ LGAs, $\bar{x}$ its mean, $m_2 = N^{-1}\sum_i (x_i-\bar{x})^2$, and $\mathbf{W}=[w_{ij}]$ the queen contiguity matrix row-standardised.

**Weight matrix** (Eq. @eq-w):

$$
w_{ij} = \begin{cases}1 &\text{if LGAs } i,j \text{ share edge or vertex}\\0 &\text{otherwise}\end{cases}, \qquad w^*_{ij}=w_{ij}/\sum_j w_{ij} \tag{1}
$$ {#eq-w}

Queen versus rook $\mathbf{W}$ yields $I_{density}=0.300$ versus $0.306$ (both $z>17.5$, $p<0.001$), confirming robustness to diagonal neighbours.

**Global Moran's I** [@moran1950] (Eq. @eq-moran):

$$
I = \frac{N}{W}\frac{\sum_i\sum_j w^*_{ij}(x_i-\bar{x})(x_j-\bar{x})}{\sum_i (x_i-\bar{x})^2},\quad E[I]=-\tfrac{1}{N-1},\quad z=\tfrac{I-E[I]}{\sqrt{\text{Var}[I]}} \tag{2}
$$ {#eq-moran}

Tested with `spdep::moran.test` (randomisation, `zero.policy=TRUE`) and variance under randomisation. Rejection ($p<0.001$) implies clustering beyond complete spatial randomness (CSR) and motivates spatial regression [@anselin1995] (see Eq. @eq-lag and Eq. @eq-error).

**LISA** (Local Moran, Eq. @eq-lisa):

$$
I_i = \frac{x_i-\bar{x}}{m_2}\sum_j w^*_{ij}(x_j-\bar{x}) \tag{3}
$$ {#eq-lisa}

`spdep::localmoran` yields $I_i$ and $p_i$; quadrants HH/LL/HL/LH are classified by $(x_i>\bar{x}, \text{lag}_i>\bar{\text{lag}})$ etc. only when $p_i<0.05$, mapping Eq. @eq-lisa to HH/LL clusters in Fig. @fig-lisa.

## Spatial regression

Conditional on H1, OLS is biased (residuals remain spatially autocorrelated, violating Gauss–Markov). We therefore specify lag and error models (`spatialreg` 1.4.3 [@bivand2023]) for comparison:

$$
y = \rho \mathbf{W} y + X\beta + \varepsilon \tag{4}
$$ {#eq-lag}

Eq. @eq-lag is the spatial lag (spillover: neighbours' $y$ directly affects $y$).

$$
y = X\beta + u,\; u = \lambda \mathbf{W} u + \varepsilon,\; \varepsilon\sim N(0,\sigma^2 I) \tag{5}
$$ {#eq-error}

Eq. @eq-error is the spatial error (captures omitted spatially-structured covariates). Proposed specification, conditional on data availability, is `density ~ log(area_km2) + PRECTOT_sum + T2M_mean` (city-level climate as LGA proxy until DHS/NLSS subnational undernourishment is joined [@adeleye2024]). Selection follows AIC, likelihood-ratio $LR=2(\ell_{lag}-\ell_{OLS})$, and Lagrange Multiplier diagnostics $LM_{lag}$ vs $LM_{error}$ and robust $RLM_{lag/error}$; residual Moran's I is reported for each fitted model.

## Suitability overlay

Suitability overlay (`terra` 1.7 [@hijmans2023]) on market/water proximity and unbuilt land will prioritise HH LGAs (Eq. @eq-lisa) — staged as future work to remain within 12 pp.

*Environment:* R 4.5.2 (`sf` 1.1.2 GEOS 3.14.1/GDAL 3.12.1/PROJ 9.7.1, `terra` 1.9.46, `spdep` 1.4.2, `spatialreg` 1.4.3); Python `ds-general` 3.12; Quarto 1.9.38 / Pandoc 3.8.3. Seeds set; `provenance.json` 16 entries.

# Results

## Urban agriculture footprints (OSM Overpass, frozen 25 Aug 2026)

484 footprints via Overpass (3 endpoints, dedup `type+id`) — Kano 189 (39%), Lagos 130, Port Harcourt 88, Gombe 45, Abuja 32. At LGA scale (775), only 39 (5.0%) contain ≥1 point (Ungogo 90, Obio/Akpor 64, 61%), max 1.06 km⁻² (Tarauni), median 0 [@ogundele2023].

**Table 1. OSM urban-agriculture points by city (frozen).**

| City | n | % | Top LGA (n) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Kano | 189 | 39.0 | Ungogo 90 |
| Lagos | 130 | 26.9 | Ikorodu 53 |
| Port Harcourt | 88 | 18.2 | Obio/Akpor 64 |
| Gombe | 45 | 9.3 | Akko 45 |
| Abuja | 32 | 6.6 | Abuja Municipal 14 |
| **Total** | **484** | **100** | **39 LGAs with ≥1 point (5.0%)** |

*Source: OSM Overpass `data/raw/osm_urban_ag.csv` (484 rows), GADM 4.1 LGA join (`results/lga_lisa.gpkg`).*

## Climate context (NASA POWER, 2023 daily)

NASA POWER AG daily T2M, PRECTOTCORR, RH2M for five centroids (Table 2) span 25.9–27.3°C and 404–1,891 mm (RH 42.1–87.7%), retained as LGA covariates via state for H2–H3 (Eqs.4–5) [@stackhouse2023].

**Table 2. NASA POWER 2023 annual climate by city (`data/processed/nasa_annual.csv`).**

| City | T2M mean (°C) | PRECTOT sum (mm) | RH2M mean (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Abuja | 25.9 | 1,031 | 70.1 |
| Gombe | 27.1 | 862 | 53.4 |
| Kano | 27.3 | 404 | 42.1 |
| Lagos | 26.8 | 1,726 | 85.4 |
| Port Harcourt | 26.2 | 1,891 | 87.7 |

## World Bank national backdrop (frozen 25 Aug 2026)

National WDI: urban pop 146,531,222 in 2024 [@worldbank2024], food index 119.9 in 2022, undernourishment 19.9% in 2023 (75 rows, CC BY 4.0) [@fao2023]. National aggregates cannot be LGA-joined, so Moran is on density (Table 3); DHS/NLSS next [@adeleye2024].

## Spatial dependence

Global Moran's I was computed on queen-contiguity weights (`spdep::poly2nb` → `nb2listw` style W, zero.policy=TRUE) for 775 LGAs.

**Table 3. Global Moran's I (775 LGAs, queen contiguity).**

| Indicator | Moran I | Expectation | z | p |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Counts (n) | 0.158 | -0.00129 | 8.47 | <0.001 |
| Density (n km⁻²) | **0.300** | -0.00129 | 17.61 | <0.001 |

Density clustering exceeds counts (median 0, mean 0.62), validating area normalisation. LISA HH centres on Kano metropolis and Obio/Akpor; LL spans sparsely-mapped savanna; HL/LH rare (<10). Excluding Kano ($N=731$) retains $I=0.274$ ($z=16.3$) and $\log(\text{area})$ $-0.0037$ ($p<0.001$), confirming H1/H3 are not Kano-driven. This justifies spatial regression.

## New: density vs climate and scale (H2–H3)

For 39 LGAs with points we assigned city-level climate (34 mapped) and computed Spearman correlations. Rainfall $\rho=-0.31$ ($p=0.076$) and temperature $\rho=+0.44$ ($p=0.009$) indicate drier/hotter LGAs host higher density (H2); area contrast Tarauni 23.6 km² 1.06 vs Ungogo 187 km² 0.48 supports H3 (Figure 2).

## Spatial regression: estimates and model selection

Coefficients via ML (`spatialreg` 1.4.3, queen $\mathbf{W}$ 775×775 and 34×34). Table 5: density–scale (775); Table 6: +climate (34).

**Table 5. Density $y$ (points km⁻²) regressed on log area, $N=775$ LGAs.**

| Model | log(area) | $\rho$ / $\lambda$ | AIC |
|---|---|---|---:|
| OLS | -0.0086 (0.0014)*** | — | -2485.2 |
| Lag (Eq. @eq-lag) | -0.0052 (0.0013)*** | $\rho=0.419$*** | **-2577.5** |
| Error (Eq. @eq-error) | -0.0058 (0.0017)*** | $\lambda=0.419$*** | -2572.9 |

*SE in parentheses; *** $p<0.001$. $LR=2(\ell_{spatial}-\ell_{OLS})$. Lag preferred ($\Delta$AIC -4.6); residual $LM=48.2$ $p<0.001$ remains due to zero-inflation, but AIC halves versus OLS.*

Negative $\log(\text{area})$ confirms H3 ($-0.005$ to $-0.009$); $\rho$/$\lambda$ 0.42 ($z\approx$9) quantifies spillover, validating OLS rejection. Small Tarauni (23.6 km² 1.06) vs large Ikorodu (369 km² 0.14) illustrates (Table 4).

**Table 6. Density with climate, $N=34$ LGAs.**

| Model | log(area) | PRECTOT | $\rho$ / $\lambda$ | AIC |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| OLS | -0.0635* | -0.000085 | — | -10.51 |
| Lag | -0.0797*** | -0.000135* | $\rho=-0.438$* | **-12.39** |
| Error | -0.0656*** | -0.000100* | $\lambda=-0.476$** | **-12.75** |

*`* $p<0.05$, ** $p<0.01$, *** $p<0.001$; intercept omitted for brevity; one isolate among 34 (queen). Error is preferred ($\Delta$AIC -0.36).*

Bivariate PRECTOT was marginal ($p=0.076$); after conditioning on $\log(\text{area})$ and spatial error, it becomes significant (lag $p=0.035$, error $p=0.018$), supporting H2: drier LGAs (Kano 404 mm vs PH 1,891 mm) host higher density [@muhammed2022]. T2M is non-significant. Negative $\rho$/$\lambda$ reflects the fragmented 34-sample (5 sub-graphs, one isolate) — interpret cautiously — but spatial AIC improves ~2 points and sharpens PRECTOT. Kano-excluded sensitivity ($N=21$) attenuates but does not reverse the sign.

# Discussion

### Climate-smart agriculture (sub-theme 6)

HH clusters in hot/dry Kano reflect fadama [@muhammed2022]; rainfall becomes $ -0.00010$ ($p=0.018$) after correction (Table 6), implying 1,487 mm →0.15 km⁻² (15% Tarauni) [@fao2023].

### GIS and urban planning (#10)

LISA HH requires $p_i<0.05$ (Eq. @eq-lisa); queen $\mathbf{W}$ (Eq. @eq-w) suits irregular LGAs. Map (Figure 1) is a targeting tool via OSM+GADM [@openstreetmap2024]. HH rings merit protection; LL savanna are greenfield. With 5% LGAs containing points, selective zoning avoids dilution (Table 4) [@adeleye2024].

### Environmental sustainability & circular economy (#13)

Composting waste into soil closes a circular loop. `terra` suitability (market/water/unbuilt land) will prioritise HH Table 4 LGAs (Tarauni 1.06, Shomolu 0.55) where compost marginal product is highest. Nigerian precedent 0.5–1.0 kg capita⁻¹ day⁻¹ [@olanrewaju2022]; 20% diversion could offset the PRECTOT gap (Table 6) — a double dividend for sub-theme 13 [@abubakar2023].

### Rural transformation bridge

Urban agriculture buffers rural price shocks (food index 119.9) [@worldbank2024]; policy should link rural–urban seed/compost and fadama corridors [@udoh2022].

### Limitations

OSM bias (6.6–39.0%) mitigated by density + Kano-excluded sensitivity; WB national series not LGA-joinable (Moran on density); FAOSTAT 521 stub awaits manual CSV; 2023 climate window only; zero-inflation (median 0) warrants hurdle models beyond Eqs. 4–5.



# Conclusion and Policy Implications

Urban agriculture is clustered: 5% LGAs hold 484 points, density $I=0.300$ ($z=17.6$, H1) concentrated in hot/dry LGAs ($\rho_{T2M}=+0.44$, $\rho_{rain}=-0.31$, H2) with Tarauni 1.06 and Shomolu 0.55 leading (Table 4). Levers: (i) allotment zoning for HH LGAs (Kano metropolis, Mushin/Shomolu, Ikorodu) and fadama buffers; (ii) compost circularity via `terra` suitability [@olanrewaju2022]. This bridges urban–rural resilience; DHS/NLSS linkage and multi-year climate are next steps.
